verdicts.what_would_bite: Nothing bites. The claim (both scripts launched by no CLI verb) is false on the current tree, and not merely on paper: executing the verbs on the fixture installed each script into the round's workflow dir with the prelude spliced and printed a Workflow call whose args satisfy each script's own required-key guard verbatim (attack-design.js:14 repo/design_path/subject/out/models/round/schema_version, its subject's five fields from schema-validated catalog/attack/<instrument>.toml; rubric-audit.js:15 subject/hats/items/personas_path/models/out/round/schema_version). Preflight.main_script (Preflight.jl:792), the line the finding cited, maps only the four instrument entry points and is not this launch path, so its being unchanged is not evidence the defect survives. verdicts.evidence: src/Scan.jl:351-353 — `id = row["id"]; rule = row["rule"]` … `for e in Ledger.entries(ledger, rule; scope = "policy")` … `e["target"] == "*" && return (Hit[], length(hits), true)`. catalog/scans.toml:206-207 — `id = "SCAN.DOI_CROSSCHECK"` / `rule = "RULE.CIT.FULL_INLINE"`. policy/RULES.toml:432,437 — `id = "RULE.CIT.DOI"` … `check = ["scan:SCAN.DOI_CROSSCHECK"]`. ARCHITECTURE §12.A:2327 — "the ledger's `scope = "policy"` entries and the scans' `rule` column cite these".
verdicts.what_would_bite: A consumer records the documented waiver `id = "RULE.CIT.DOI", scope = "policy", target = "*"`. CFG.EXEMPTIONS accepts it (Doctor.jl:340, the id is in RULES.toml), EXEMPT.STALE passes it (Doctor.jl:380, target `*` returns true), and Sync.deviations (Sync.jl:104) renders it into .gbg/policy/deviations.md as a granted deviation — but Scan.apply_ledger looks policy entries up under the scalar row["rule"] = RULE.CIT.FULL_INLINE only, so nothing matches and the DOI half of the hard scan (doi_crosscheck.jl's `require_doi` branch, "a reference without a DOI or Open Library link on its title") keeps failing the gate: a silently void waiver on the rule whose ONLY declared check is that scan. The mirror case over-reaches: a policy waiver on RULE.CIT.FULL_INLINE disables the whole scan and withdraws RULE.CIT.DOI enforcement nobody exempted. Same shape on SCAN.DEAD_REF (column RULE.DOC.NO_DEAD_REFS; RULE.CIT.NO_INACCESSIBLE unwaivable) and SCAN.API_PAGE_STRUCTURE (RULE.DOC.API_GROUPING waivable for its sibling HTML scans but not this one). The accepted remedy — a scans.toml header telling a reader to consult §12.B — never touches the engine that resolves waivers through the column, and the dismissal's mechanism ("a SCALAR by schema") is unbacked: schema/ holds no scans schema; scan_catalog() is a bare TOML.parsefile.

verdicts.evidence: Only readers of cfg["docs"]: retired_claims.jl:6, html_base_leak.jl:6, html_public_home.jl:11, Sync.jl:136 — never doctest; the ext does "result = Documenter.makedocs(; kwargs...)". latex_source_globs occurs only at schema/config.schema.json:441 and Init.jl:163; panel.js:86 hardcodes "the docstrings under ${A.repo}/src/ and ${A.repo}/ext/, the pages under ${A.repo}/docs/src/". §5.5's list names neither key.
verdicts.what_would_bite: PF's config (ARCHITECTURE:1241) sets latex_source_globs = ["src/*.jl", "examples/*.jl"]; `gbg preflight check-consistency` renders args with no source field (instruments/check-consistency/schema.json has no such property), so panel.js hands the latex-typesetter hat only the hardcoded src/, ext/, docs/src/, docs/ — examples/, the Literate surface where display math lives, is silently never read, while the hat is required to quote findings at their source file:line. Symmetrically, IT's docs.doctest = false (ARCHITECTURE:1316) is ignored: the class-S seed templates/make.jl.seed:14 passes doctest = true and the wrapper forwards kwargs verbatim, so doctests run anyway with no warning. The dismissal's rationale only half-holds: docs/make.jl is a consumer-owned seed, so doctest does have a competing home, but latex_source_globs has none — its would-be home is a hardcoded path list inside a Workflow script, which CLAUDE.md's core invariant forbids ("No package string, path or round datum in a Workflow script"), so that key is fixable in-round without touching any closed set. And §5.5 (read in full, ARCHITECTURE:1371-1386) names neither key, while ARCHITECTURE:2151-2154 lists both among admitted config keys, so "dropping them is MAJOR under §5.5's closed non-configurable set" is not supported by the cited text. Every sibling key of both tables has a reader (retired_claims, unexported_base_expected, admonition_titles, profile/hats/core/domain_hats/seed_catalog, design_docs_withheld at Rounds.jl:111 and Passes.jl:570); these two do not — that asymmetry is the finding, and no test asserts either key.

verdicts.what_would_bite: The dismissal rests on "both unlisted edits are individually sound". templates/README.md's edit checks out (templates/SKILL.md.tmpl carries `<!-- gbg:managed ... -->` on line 6, after the YAML frontmatter; templates/queue-guard.sh.tmpl carries none). install.md's does not: a site reader meets a definition enumerating exactly five consumers at line 8 and, three paragraphs later at lines 39-41, "One consumer is routed differently: a consumer pinned at `dev` that is not itself the tool's checkout — the fixture" — a consumer the new sentence excludes. The same closed-vocabulary claim also gains a third home (policy/glossary.md:3, rendered at docs/src/guide/rules.md:647, now guide/install.md:8) with no link to the home, which is the class catalog/lanes/check-docs.toml's `one-home` lane exists to catch. "Unfixable in place" holds only for the pushed commit message; the prose the unmentioned edit put in the tree is editable today, and the dismissal never examined it against the page it landed on.
